spatial_claims.claim: Point A lies on plane Π; two distinct rays AB and AC emanate from A, both perpendicular to Π, both on the same side
Lines AB and AC are parallel, by 11.6 applied to their mutual perpendicularity to Π
Lines AB and AC both pass through point A, contradicting parallelism (D1.23)

configuration_map: Point A: lies on plane Π (fixed throughout). Line through AB: perpendicular to Π, passes through A. Line through AC: perpendicular to Π, passes through A, distinct from line through AB. No auxiliary points constructed. No angles decomposed. No interior/exterior claims made. The configuration is minimal: a single point on a plane with two lines through it, both perpendicular to the plane.
pass_reason: The proof makes minimal spatial claims (two lines from A perpendicular to a plane, their parallelism via 11.6, their intersection at A). These claims are deliberately contradictory as part of the reductio argument — that is the intended structure, not a configuration error. No auxiliary constructions, angle decompositions, or interior/exterior arguments introduce hidden inconsistencies. The logical chain (perpendicularity to same plane implies parallelism by 11.6; parallelism implies non-intersection by D1.23; but both lines pass through A) is spatially coherent.
